title: Multiplexed token-aware reranker with adaptive per-candidate timeouts
creator: Aisha R. Patel
description:
Problem: The reranking endpoint is seeing tail latency spikes when candidate sets contain variable-length contexts. Long candidates (or large prompt prefixes) block microbatches and force conservative global timeouts, hurting throughput and quality for the majority of short candidates.

Proposal: Implement a multiplexed scoring path that: (1) computes token budgets per candidate and places candidates into fast/standard/slow lanes, (2) runs fast-lane candidates in parallel with tighter per-candidate soft timeouts and earlier early-exit heuristics, (3) streams partial scores for early-stop candidates to the caller when below a confidence threshold, and (4) applies token-aware backpressure so long candidates do not stall smaller ones. This combines adaptive per-candidate timeouts, dynamic microbatch composition, and a non-blocking aggregator to reduce p95/p99 latency while preserving quality for long candidates.

Non-goals: full model architecture changes (quantization/weights), changing customer-facing API shape, or replacing existing KV cache behavior. This is an operational/runtime enhancement on top of current reranker models.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for rerank endpoint reduced by >=30% on the mixed-length benchmark compared to baseline (current prod).
p99 latency reduced by >=20% without increasing average token cost per request by more than 8%.
end-to-end correctness: scores ordering preserved for a 95% sampled prompt set (no regressions with statistical significance > 1%).
graceful fallback: if multiplexing fails, system falls back to existing single-path reranker with metrics indicating fallback rate.
observability: new dashboards showing lane composition, per-candidate timeouts fired, partial score stream rate, and backpressure events.
automated canary: safety checks run for 48 hours on 5% traffic with automated rollback on SLA breaches.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha R. Patel: Initial draft ticket created after spike. Benchmarks show median candidate length is 56 tokens but 5% of candidates exceed 120 tokens causing blocking in microbatches.

2026-02-26 - Mateo Gonzalez: Spike implementation completed (local): proof-of-concept multiplexing using a 3-lane scheduler. Short stage reduces p95 by ~28% on synthetic mix. Integrating aggregator next.

2026-03-02 - Design review: PM and infra requested explicit fallback metrics and a canary plan. Decided to stream partial scores as proto messages over existing HTTP2 chunking instead of changing API shape.

2026-03-07 - Performance update: integrated KV cache awareness into lane assignment; candidates with hot prefixes bias to fast lane. Observed 5% extra token reads due to prefetch, acceptable under cost SLO.
2026-03-12 - Security/Infra: No KMS or secrets changes required. Added rollout gating to prevent multiplexer on Dedicated pools until load-testing is green.
testing_plan: Unit tests for lane assignment logic and timeout scheduler (edge cases: zero-length candidate, extreme-length candidate).
Integration test with existing KV cache: ensure cache hits maintain lane affinity.
Load test: 10k qps synthetic mix with 10/60/30 short/medium/long candidate distribution; collect p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
Canary: 5% of prod traffic for 48 hours on hosted API; automated SLA checks and anomaly detection on score distribution drift.
Chaos test: kill a scoring worker to validate aggregator fallback and no request-level hangs.
monitoring: alert: p99 increase > 25% vs baseline for 5m
rollout_plan: 0% - merge behind feature flag in runtime and serving (unit/integration tests pass).
5% - canary on hosted API (48h) with automated rollback on SLA breaches.
25% - expand canary after cost/quality verification; enable partial-score streaming for eligible SDKs.
50% - enable on staging Dedicated pools and a subset of enterprise customers under feature flag.
100% - enable globally after 7 days of stable metrics and PM sign-off.
risks: Score drift: early-exit heuristics could change ranking distribution; mitigated by shadow runs and score-preservation checks.
Cost increase: prefetching and multiplex orchestration can increase token reads; capped by token-budget heuristics and config knobs.
Interaction with autoscaling: lane imbalance could spike GPU utilization in certain pools; coordinate with infra autoscaler and add lane-aware scaling signals.
Telemetry gap: new partial streams need end-to-end tracing; ensure trace ids flow through aggregator and client SDK.
complexity_and_workaround: Medium-high complexity due to scheduler changes and aggregator semantics. Short-term workaround: implement a 'short-candidate fast path' only (no full multiplexing) to gain partial p95 benefits while we harden streaming aggregator.
notes: Owner: Mateo for implementation, Aisha for product acceptance, Jun Park for observability dashboards.
